title: Duas das três páginas do registo nacional não devolvem texto a um leitor automático
title_en: Two of the three national registry pages return no text to a machine reader

extraction.note: Entities and edges proposed by a Claude Code session reading the article and its afirmacoes.json, against the published article ontology. No human has reviewed this extraction. Errors here propagate into every explanation downstream, which is why the review status is carried on the page rather than in a footnote.

what_it_says: Three pages of Portugal's public registry were requested the way any program would request them — one HTTP request, no scripts run — and the bytes kept. The official gazette returned 2,346 bytes and 22 characters of visible text. The government page returned 165,569 bytes and 348 characters. The national open-data portal returned 849,388 bytes and 27,406 characters, and is the only one of the three a machine reader can read. A measurement on published artefacts, with a date and a hash, not an opinion about anyone.

consequence_connections.reads: The risk owner watches who is answerable; a registry of record that is unreadable to any non-browser client creates an accessibility and machine-readability exposure for the body that publishes it, whoever else it also affects.
consequence_connections.reads_inverse: This weakness makes the publishing bodies answerable, which the risk owner watches.
